record.description: Every content-derived value an Audit Record seals is a commitment keyed by the salt of the audit's Reference Payload — the anchor as of `reference_delta` (WIST-4 §5), never a bare digest: withdrawing that Payload destroys the salt and renders these commitments uncheckable at the same instant as the Delta's own.

reference_delta.description: The Delta the audit measured against: the newest Delta of the audited Delta's per-URL chain sealed at or before `fetched_at` (WIST-4 §5). It fixes the Reference Payload and therefore the salt every commitment below is keyed by; it is never before `audited_delta` in the chain, and where the chain had not advanced by the fetch it equals `audited_delta`.

auditor_id.description: The hostname the Auditor was admitted under: WIST-4 §3 requires it to be byte-identical to the `subject` of the `auditor_admit` covering `sig.key_id`, and the pattern is the one that `subject` carries, so a Record cannot claim a shape no admission could have.

fetched_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC at whole-second precision with a literal trailing Z, the form block.schema.json fixes for `sealed_at`. WIST-4 §3 has every validator recomputing reputation reject a Record whose `fetched_at` falls outside the closed interval between two Block `sealed_at` values, so the field is compared against Block timestamps by every replaying party and is written in the one form they carry.

robots_excluded.description: Present only on an `unreachable` Record whose fetch was forbidden by robots.txt (WIST-4 §5); it is what the unauditable horizon counts, so it distinguishes a URL nobody may check from one that was merely down.

prev_record.description: The ID of this Auditor's immediately preceding Audit Record or coverage_attestation published for the same Log, or null for its first there (WIST-4 §4). The chain is per (Auditor, Log), because every state derived from it is (WIST-3 §8). The per-auditor chain is what turns a selectively suppressed submission into proof of its own existence: a sealed successor naming an unsealed predecessor demonstrates the predecessor was published.

then.comment: similarity is required for every change type alike, `delete` included: what the change type adjusts is the reading (WIST-4 §5's effective similarity), never the presence of the field, which is what keeps §7's severity derivable for every Confirmed Inconsistency. link_variance and link_inconsistent both obtained a representation and a measured extract similarity (WIST-4 §5: only a consistent-band extract can yield a link verdict), so they carry the same commitments.

allOf.comment: robots_excluded says why a fetch produced no representation, so it belongs to `unreachable` and to nothing else: on any other verdict a representation was obtained (WIST-4 §5), and on `not_auditable` the obstacle was the Reference Payload rather than the URL.

A link verdict asserts a link_agreement reading, so the Record must seal it; on the other measured verdicts the field is present when the link dimension applied and absent when it was neutral (a non-HTML representation, or a delete audit — WIST-4 §5).
